name: Cloudflare creation benchmark
purpose: Six real user journeys map the twelve wishlist themes to observable outcomes. This file defines work; reading it runs nothing. No full journey, cloud result, baseline score or agent comparison has been recorded here.

foundation.rule: Only named source-function checks are runnable through the foundation. A pass does not qualify browser persistence, IAM, Cloudflare execution, billing, audiovisual proof or any complete journey.
foundation.sourceReferenceRule: sourceCheckProvenance names original source checks, not runnable selectors. The foundation module emits prefixed check IDs; use its actual results for selection and evidence.

coveragePolicy.themeRule: Theme tags describe relevance, not certification. CF-05 has a separate optional Artifacts profile; all other themes map to required journeys.
coveragePolicy.denominatorRule: Always show all six required journeys. An optional profile cannot satisfy, remove or reduce required coverage. Declare variants before running and retain missing variants.
coveragePolicy.layerRule: Keep local-helper, actual-browser, controlled-provider, isolated-cloud and actual-agent evidence separate. Simulation cannot establish provider behaviour.

runPrerequisites: Pin campaign/case definitions, source and deployment revisions, fixtures, independent expected states, dependencies and runner versions.
Declare target account/project/environment, allowed effects, task allowance, timeout/retry/fallback policy and cleanup ownership.
Use synthetic or rights-cleared inputs and disposable resources. Cloud access, paid calls and publication require their actual supported scope and authorisation.

Inject faults only in owned disposable targets. A production-labelled negative case uses a disposable sentinel or non-executing plan fixture. Inspect actual production bindings read-only and stop if a real production target appears; never route a test mutation there.

Bound revocation, lost-acknowledgement and allowance experiments by explicit requests, duration and independent resource/spend ceilings. Use no-charge fixtures where possible; never test uncontrolled overspend.
Missing runners, accounts or capabilities remain blocked/not-run. No silent account, provider, modality or paid fallback.
Use existing #601 runner/results ownership. This campaign adds no dashboard, scheduler or blanket release gate.

resultPolicy.passRule: The legitimate user outcome completes, required invariants pass, independent evidence matches the actual target and cleanup is accounted for.
hardFailures: Lost protected state or unauthorised republication
resultPolicy.stopRule: Stop and report the affected trial on a hard failure; other successes cannot average it away.
resultPolicy.positiveControlRule: A valid corresponding action must succeed; denying everything cannot satisfy the journey.
resultPolicy.uncertaintyRule: Safe uncertainty handling can pass an invariant while the user task remains blocked. Unknown is not success, zero cost or proof of no effect.
resultPolicy.reportRule: Show task status, invariant results, evidence layer and observed metrics separately. Preserve all attempts and denominators; no universal 100-point score or helper-check count presented as completed journeys.

missingHandling.null-with-reason: Keep the value null and explain the missing observation. Never substitute zero, an estimate, a simulated amount or a successful-only sample.

measurementPolicy.costRule: Currency metrics require a currency code, amount basis and source. Separate observed charges, estimates, reservations and simulations; subscription entitlement is not API credit.
measurementPolicy.comparisonRule: Use at least three fresh repeats per compared configuration with frozen inputs, expected states, permissions, budget and toolchain. Preserve failures and reset owned state between attempts.
measurementPolicy.agentRule: When used, record actual model/provider, resolved route, harness, prompt/skills, tools and grants. An API model is not credited with a separate harness’s actions.
measurementPolicy.timingRule: Record setup and complete task time separately, actual device/viewport/location, cache state and network conditions. Australian latency needs corresponding measurements.
measurementPolicy.statisticsRule: Retain raw values; with small samples show count, median and range rather than stable-tail or superiority claims.
measurementPolicy.humanRule: Keep attributed, append-only human observations separate from deterministic correctness. Blind paired reviews when appropriate; no generated approval.

requiredEvidenceForEveryRun: Runner/profile, target identity and effective grants without secrets
Trace/receipts with failure and uncertainty details
Measured values with units and missing reasons

findingClassification.rule: Allow multiple contributors. Platform feedback needs the exact operation/version/plan and a reproduction or explicit documented constraint. Existing functionality we misuse belongs to our implementation; misleading discovery belongs to docs. Missing access is not a missing platform feature.
findingClassification.exportRule: Send measured workaround burden and the smallest supported request. Keep general aspirations outside strict repo findings and sanitise evidence before sharing.

cases.name: Create an app and reopen the result
cases.expectedOutcome: A creator makes a useful app for a declared task, saves and reopens it, makes a second useful change and retains owned source plus the supported saved state with truthful receipts.
prerequisites: Choose a real app/blueprint and freeze its supported field contract.
Use a clean disposable workspace and an independent expected-state fixture.
Define the useful task and first/second expected changes before running; choose a supported source-export path.
cases.input: Fixed name, description, layout/theme and link edits plus one supported persisted interaction.
orderedProcedure: Record clean state, the intended user task and setup time.
Inspect the intended changes and required authority.
Create the useful app and apply the fixed first edits through the actual interface; save.
Close/reopen and compare authoritative stored fields and the supported interaction with expected state.
Make a second useful change through the reopened interface; save, reopen and independently verify it.
Export owned source and supported saved state; re-import supported fields and inspect omissions, source identity and both changes.

positiveControl.action: Complete the declared app task, save and reopen, then make the second useful change.
positiveControl.expected: Both intended changes persist, the interaction works, and the creator retains usable source and the supported export.

negativeCases.inject: Display success while retaining initial state.
negativeCases.expected: Independent state comparison fails.

negativeCases.inject: Use an unsupported version/field or publication state.
negativeCases.expected: Refuse or explicitly bound the import without partial corruption.

evidenceRequired: Retained owned source and declared usable scope

cases.name: Preview a change with bounded delegated access
cases.expectedOutcome: A colleague or agent creates and uses a correctly isolated preview within its grant; unrelated resources stay protected and revocation is observable.
prerequisites: Two owned disposable projects with distinct test identities/grants, including a disposable production-labelled sentinel or non-executing production plan fixture.
Declare every dependency target, required isolation and cleanup ownership.
Declare revocation semantics for new requests, sessions and running work.
cases.input: A bounded colleague preview grant and fixed change; the second disposable project and production-labelled sentinel remain outside its scope. Actual production is never a mutation target.
orderedProcedure: Inspect the plan, permissions and complete declared dependency inventory; inspect live bindings read-only and stop on any actual production mapping.
Block paths whose required isolation cannot be established.
Complete the valid preview task and inspect its effect.
Attempt the equivalent action only against the prohibited disposable test project or production-labelled sentinel; use a non-executing plan fixture if no safe sentinel exists.
Revoke only the disposable test grant; test subsequent access and declared in-flight behaviour within the fixed allowance.
Remove only the run’s owned resources.

positiveControl.action: Run the valid action with correctly isolated targets and a valid grant.
positiveControl.expected: The intended preview works; a deny-all implementation cannot pass.

negativeCases.inject: Target the second owned disposable test project/environment outside the test grant.
negativeCases.expected: Deny the action and leave the protected target unchanged.

negativeCases.inject: Withhold required binding visibility.
negativeCases.expected: Expose incomplete coverage and block the isolation-dependent path.

negativeCases.inject: Declare a disposable sentinel labelled production in the plan, or supply a non-executing production-target fixture; never address actual production.
negativeCases.expected: Reject it before execution.

negativeCases.inject: Reuse the disposable test grant after the declared revocation boundary against owned test resources only.
negativeCases.expected: Deny further work according to the documented coverage; old receipts confer no authority.

cases.name: Recover an interrupted stateful change
cases.expectedOutcome: A stale observation or lost acknowledgement does not cause an unexpected overwrite or duplicate effect; recovery restores its declared scope while retaining current restrictions.
prerequisites: A disposable stateful app with an explicit recovery boundary.
Freeze expected source/data versions, fault points and moderation states.
Declare conditional-write, idempotency and reconciliation support for the exact operation.
Fault injection and the second actor operate only on disposable owned resources with bounded attempts; no real customer jobs or external recipients.
cases.input: A saved content revision, later content edit and newer hidden/pending states; a separately controlled actor and acknowledgement-loss point.
orderedProcedure: Observe state, then change the guarded version with the second test actor.
Attempt the original change and inspect the conflict or documented alternative.
In a reset variant, complete one effect and lose its acknowledgement.
Resume with the same operation identity and reconcile before retrying.
Rehearse the declared code/data recovery on disposable resources.
Reopen and compare restored content, current moderation and effect counts.

positiveControl.action: Apply and recover the valid supported change without injected faults.
positiveControl.expected: The intended content is restored and protected records remain hidden/pending.

negativeCases.inject: Modify state between observation and mutation.
negativeCases.expected: Do not silently overwrite the unexpected version or call a snapshot atomic.

negativeCases.inject: Complete an effect but lose its response.
negativeCases.expected: Reconcile before retry; unresolved completion stays explicitly unresolved.

negativeCases.inject: Supply incompatible saved state.
negativeCases.expected: Reject or recover within the declared contract without half-applying.

negativeCases.inject: Restore a snapshot predating a moderation restriction.
negativeCases.expected: Do not silently republish currently restricted material.

evidenceRequired: Authoritative final state and effect counts

currentFoundationSupport.establishes: Limited launchpad restoration and moderation behaviour.

cases.name: Finish a budgeted media job and reuse its output
cases.expectedOutcome: An approved original survives transfer interruption, runs on a compatible processor and exports with intact lineage, permitted visibility and truthful cost attribution.
prerequisites: Pin rights-cleared original bytes, processing recipe and expected output.
Declare runtime/native dependencies, duration/memory, persistence/network/location needs.
Use installed deterministic processing first; paid generation is not required.
Fix the allowance, concurrency, currency/resource units and permitted overshoot before execution.
Use a disposable test project and independent request/resource ceiling for unknown-cost and concurrency variants; if a safe bound is unavailable, mark blocked before execution.
cases.input: A fixed original, supported transform and export recipe; interruption point and explicit cost/allowance policy.
orderedProcedure: Check runtime eligibility and record the estimate and its scope.
Interrupt the actual upload; resume if supported, otherwise report the limitation.
Verify accepted bytes and project/asset identity.
Run the fixed transform; qualify and attribute any fallback.
Exercise the fixed concurrency/allowance within the independent ceiling; stop at the bound and reconcile any ambiguous job result.
Validate output and reopen its exported source/variant pack.
Record observed charges separately from estimates, reservations and unknowns.

positiveControl.action: Transfer/process/export the supported original with valid authority.
positiveControl.expected: Validated output retains its source relationships and stays within the declared allowance contract.

negativeCases.inject: Mismatch source hash or size.
negativeCases.expected: Do not accept it as the intended revision.

negativeCases.inject: Stop at a fixed upload boundary.
negativeCases.expected: Preserve identity through supported resumption or report blocked; no false completion.

negativeCases.inject: Delay or omit charge information in the controlled test observation; use a no-charge fixture or independently bounded authorised job.
negativeCases.expected: Keep cost unknown, not zero; apply the declared allowance policy.

negativeCases.inject: Remove a required runtime capability.
negativeCases.expected: Block or use an independently qualified, disclosed fallback.

negativeCases.inject: Drop an expected source/variant link.
negativeCases.expected: Export verification detects the loss.

currentFoundationSupport.establishes: Provider-helper handling of unknown cost only.

cases.name: Prove the real game or listening experience
cases.expectedOutcome: A meaningful game or listening interaction has version-linked visual/audio evidence and independently verified state, with capture limits disclosed.
prerequisites: Declare game/audio variants and required tracks before running.
Pin actual app/version, approved content, browser/device, viewport and location.
Choose capture capable of the required pixels and sound; DOM replay alone is insufficient for omitted content.
Assign a human reviewer for a separately attributed assessment of the actual result; do not substitute a model claim of human experience.
cases.input: A fixed game interaction or start/navigate/seek playback journey on a real owned product, with an independent expected state.
orderedProcedure: Verify target version and capture capability.
Perform the fixed interaction and record authoritative state changes.
Inspect the rendered scene, relevant sound and required timing.
Detect missing tracks or wrong-build evidence.
Attach the actual environment and a separately attributed human assessment of the real experience; retain subjective observations separately from objective assertions.
Export only approved redacted evidence and close owned capture resources.

positiveControl.action: Capture known supported content while completing the valid interaction.
positiveControl.expected: Required pixels/sound are present and actual app state confirms the interaction.

negativeCases.inject: Supply replay missing required canvas/WebGL or media content.
negativeCases.expected: Audiovisual evidence stays unqualified.

negativeCases.inject: Substitute an attractive static or unrelated prerecorded result.
negativeCases.expected: Independent interaction/state verification fails.

negativeCases.inject: Attach another build’s recording.
negativeCases.expected: Reject the identity mismatch.

negativeCases.inject: Omit required sound or break specified playback continuity.
negativeCases.expected: Report failure; a video container alone is not proof.

evidenceRequired: Separate human assessment of the real result, with reviewer identity/role disclosed only as authorised

cases.name: Continue the project as an independent owner
cases.expectedOutcome: An independent owner deploys the permitted source, supported state and assets in their own authorised account, rebinds credentials, completes the original task and makes a second useful change without hidden dependence on the original owner.
prerequisites: A supported export/reconstruction path and a separate destination account controlled by an independent owner, with explicit authority to deploy and rebind credentials. Missing access means blocked, not optional.
Pin the supported-field/resource manifest, original useful task, required second change and expected destination behaviour.
Keep the original available throughout destination validation. A different provider is not required; distinct authorised ownership and actual destination deployment are required.
cases.input: An owned app/project pack with source/data/asset manifests, declared omissions and a destination without Loftwah-only credentials.
orderedProcedure: Export permitted source, supported state and assets; inspect unsupported scope.
Reconstruct and deploy in the independent owner's authorised destination account with credentials rebound through its owning connection mechanism.
Verify supported records, relationships and permissions, then complete the original useful task against the actual destination deployment.
Make a second useful change as the destination owner; save, reopen or redeploy as required, and independently verify the resulting state.
Demonstrate that declared functionality does not use the original owner's credentials; remove only disposable test access, never the original owner's live grants.
Clean up only explicitly selected run-owned disposable resources after validation; retain the original creator work.

positiveControl.action: Deploy and operate the supported pack under the independent destination owner, then make the required second useful change.
positiveControl.expected: The actual destination completes both tasks, preserves supported data relationships and uses only its authorised credentials.

negativeCases.inject: Withhold original-owner credentials from the disposable destination; revoke only run-owned test grants, never live owner grants.
negativeCases.expected: Declared independent functionality still works or its unmet dependency is exposed.

negativeCases.inject: Request an unsupported resource/state transfer.
negativeCases.expected: State the gap; do not claim a complete backup or migration.

negativeCases.inject: Supply incompatible or unauthorised publication state.
negativeCases.expected: Refuse or bound it without corrupting the destination.

evidenceRequired: Actual destination state and reopened edit
Actual independent deployment receipt and target version
Original task and second useful change observed at the destination

currentFoundationSupport.establishes: Supported launchpad blueprint fields and disclosed omissions.

optionalProfiles.name: Optional Artifacts local event qualification
optionalProfiles.scope: Only when Artifacts is actually selected for an experimental workspace. GitHub or another supported source can remain authoritative.
prerequisites: Pin simulator/tool versions and the relevant event contract.
Use disposable local repos/workflows; remote comparison needs a separate authorised target.
orderedProcedure: Create/fork, edit and push the fixed repository fixture.
Observe actual events and build/preview workflow transitions.
Inject a delivery failure and inspect supported recovery.
Compare with the declared remote contract only if independently authorised and run.
optionalProfiles.positiveControl: A supported local operation produces its expected observable event/state.
negativeCases: Missing local events remain unsupported/unverified, not fabricated.
A failed delivery cannot be called a completed workflow.
optionalProfiles.notApplicableRule: May be marked not-applicable only when this adapter is excluded by the declared scope. Keep that status visible separately; it cannot reduce the six-case denominator or qualify CF-05.
